title: Pinsent Masons forges strategic partnership with Legora
author: Pinsent Masons

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: Pinsent Masons directly supports the proposition that deployment alone is insufficient: expansion is phased and conditional on proving use cases, while lawyer-led peer training is intended to support implementation. Its claims about faster meaningful results remain predictive and unquantified, consistent with the synthesis’s distinction between adoption and demonstrated outcomes.
qs: This partnership will bring the firm’s total number of Legora users to 1,000, with plans to expand this further as use cases are proven.
The successful implementation of Legora will be supported by the firm’s expanding cohort of AI Champions, lawyers from associate through to partner who will be trained to upskill their colleagues.

kp.k: Global AI rollout follows a structured practice-group pilot
kp.d: Pinsent Masons announced a global strategic partnership with Legora on 23 Feb 2026 following a pilot in corporate, commercial and property. Deployment will extend globally within those teams, while remaining practice groups begin pilots. The announcement says the partnership will bring Legora users to 1,000; further expansion is conditional on proving use cases, rather than an already completed firmwide deployment.
qs: Following the successful pilot, Legora will now be rolled out globally across the firm’s corporate, commercial and property teams, with pilots set to commence in all remaining practice groups.
This partnership will bring the firm’s total number of Legora users to 1,000, with plans to expand this further as use cases are proven.

kp.k: Collaboration targets research, drafting and review workflows
kp.d: The announcement describes Legora as a collaborative workspace intended to streamline research, drafting and review. It frames the partnership as joint exploration and development of legal workflows to enhance client experience, explicitly contrasting this approach with simply deploying off-the-shelf tools.
qs: Legora is a collaborative AI workspace built to fit seamlessly into a lawyer’s workflow and works to streamline everything from research to drafting and review.

Sharing the mindset that meaningful innovation is driven through collaboration with developers, not by simply deploying off the shelf tools, Pinsent Masons and Legora will work together to accelerate the exploration of AI's applications across legal workflows.
The partnership is centred on co creating new ways to enhance the client experience.

kp.k: Lawyer champions will support peer training
kp.d: Implementation will rely on an expanding cohort of AI Champions spanning associate to partner levels, who will be trained to upskill colleagues. Change & Innovation Board head Clare Francis frames the initiative as equipping lawyers to work confidently with AI and complementing their skills, rather than merely acquiring technology.
qs: The successful implementation of Legora will be supported by the firm’s expanding cohort of AI Champions, lawyers from associate through to partner who will be trained to upskill their colleagues.
This partnership shows that our focus isn’t on simply adopting technology, but on equipping our people to work confidently and creatively with it.
The pilot has allowed us to explore how this technology can complement our lawyers’ skills, helping us deliver smarter, faster and more meaningful outcomes for clients.

kp.k: Client value pressure shapes phased implementation
kp.d: Director of Transformation Neil Green says clients face pressure to demonstrate greater value through technology, which shaped the firm's approach. He reports that the structured pilot rapidly identified effective use cases and predicts that this clarity will accelerate meaningful results from phased implementation. These are management claims and expectations; the announcement supplies no quantified performance results.
qs: We know that our clients are under pressure to demonstrate greater value through the use of technology and this understanding provided the foundation for how we approached the Legora relationship, with a clear mandate to explore how it could make the greatest impact.
Our structured pilot was developed with colleagues in corporate, commercial and property and enabled us to rapidly pinpoint effective use cases.
That clarity means our subsequent phased firmwide implementation will deliver meaningful results far more quickly.

kp.k: Vendor reports platform refinement through customer engagement
kp.d: Legora's Head of Legal Engineering, Alex Fortescue-Webb, attributes platform refinement and accelerated joint progress to Pinsent Masons' structured pilot methodology and engagement. This is the vendor representative's account of collaboration, not an independently measured finding about legal-work quality or productivity.
qs: Their structured methodology, coupled with an unwavering commitment to building a true partnership, made working with them both energising and rewarding.
That level of engagement enabled us to fine tune the platform in ways that directly supported their priorities and accelerated what we could achieve together.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Pinsent Masons presents Legora as a tool for streamlining legal workflows and augmenting lawyers, with collaborative development intended to improve client outcomes.
pts.d: The announcement claims that Legora streamlines research, drafting and review. Clare Francis, Head of the Change & Innovation Board, describes AI as complementing lawyers’ skills and helping deliver smarter and faster client outcomes, rather than replacing lawyers. Director of Transformation Neil Green predicts that the effective use cases identified through the structured pilot will enable phased implementation to deliver meaningful results more quickly. Legora’s Head of Legal Engineering, Alex Fortescue-Webb, says the collaboration has already enabled platform refinements aligned with the firm’s priorities and accelerated joint progress. These are claims about workflow improvement and implementation, not quantified claims about productivity, cost reductions or staffing displacement.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered is the firm’s pilot experience and qualitative testimony from firm and vendor leaders.
pts.d: Pinsent Masons describes an extensive, successful pilot across its corporate, commercial and property groups. Green says this identified effective use cases; Francis describes exploration of how AI complements lawyers; Fortescue-Webb reports platform refinement through collaboration. The announcement does not identify particular use cases, pilot duration, performance measurements, comparative benchmarks or independently assessed client outcomes. The planned total of 1,000 users indicates deployment scale, not measured effectiveness.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 23 February 2026 announcement sets out a phased global rollout, with further expansion conditional on proven use cases and supported by training.
pts.d: The pilot precedes the announcement. Global rollout is now planned for corporate, commercial and property teams, while pilots are to begin in all other practice groups. The partnership is expected to bring total Legora users to 1,000, with expansion beyond that conditional on proving use cases. No completion date or quantified timeframe for benefits is given. The source links faster results to structured piloting and presents developer collaboration and colleague upskilling as implementation supports.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate affected groups are Pinsent Masons’ lawyers, its clients and Legora’s platform-development team.
pts.d: Lawyers in corporate, commercial and property are the first global rollout population, with other practices entering pilots. Associates through partners will act as AI Champions to train colleagues, and lawyers are expected to gain enhanced capabilities in research, drafting and review. Clients are the intended beneficiaries of improved service; Green links the initiative to clients’ pressure to demonstrate greater value through technology. Legora benefits from collaboration that informs platform refinement. The announcement does not claim effects on legal employment levels, market-wide competition or access to justice.
